working_geometry_plain: The working Phase 2 geometry is PEPS3D-anchored finite response-quotient carrier geometry. After Z, active-pair deleted masks have finite collision/residue partitions. This candidate applies one finite row-deletion operation epsilon_p to those partitions and asks which active collision survives. It does not claim topology, all-subset minimality, restoration, inverse, full coordinate coverage, or downstream geometry.

candidate_maps_considered.candidate_name: finite row-deletion collision survival over Z active collision partitions
candidate_maps_considered.finite_map: Y_row_deletion_collision_stability_K : (Z_active_pair_collision_residue_K, U_loss_pair_support_mask_K, epsilon_p:Pairs(C_Q)->Pairs(C_Q)\{p}, kappa_Z) -> finite row-deletion collision-survival table + remaining-coordinate coverage vector + F-boundary no-collision controls
why_admissible: It ratchets directly from Z by adding an explicit finite row-deletion operation epsilon_p over the three U class-pair rows.
The operation is finite: three removable rows times three active collision partitions, with F-boundary no-collision controls.
The output is finite: collision survives/breaks table, remaining coordinate coverage vector, removed-row sensitivity profile, and finite controls.
It remains PEPS3D-anchor explicit because row deletion acts on Z collision classes whose members are inherited V/E/F/C support-mask rows.
It is not topology, all-subset minimality, restore/inverse, or downstream geometry; it is only a finite deletion-sensitivity readout over Z partitions.
candidate_maps_considered.geometry_it_would_earn_if_later_passed: A bounded finite row-deletion sensitivity readout for the Phase 2 collision-residue carrier: each removed U class-pair row preserves exactly one active collision partition and breaks the other two, while remaining coordinate coverage stays V/E/C with F neutral.

candidate_maps_considered.why_deferred: Complement coordinates were already read out by Z; a standalone complement table risks summary-only status unless a later operation uses it.

candidate_maps_considered.why_rejected: Y deletes one class-pair row at a time from Z partitions. It does not test all subsets or prove minimality.
Row-deletion sensitivity of finite partitions is not topology, sheaf, homology, persistence, or closure.
Deleting rows and observing broken/surviving collisions does not restore deleted information or provide an inverse.
Hopf/Weyl, terrain, substages, flux, Xi/Phi0, Axis0, physics, IGT, and axes 7-12 remain blocked consumers.
